notes: Multiple overlapping serial systems; the page advises using data-plate MFR date, ANSI standard date, condition and appearance to disambiguate overlapping styles. Page Style 1 (2002 onward) is documented as used under the Trane, American Standard, Ameristar and Ingersoll Rand names; the page also names GE among brands under which these styles appear. Known-context correction: the page documents the letter-year system from 1983 (not from 1987) through 2001, then the year-first digit system from 2002. Parent per the page header is Ingersoll Rand; the page history notes the 2020 rename to Trane Technologies. SHIPPED (image-pass Nov 8): page Styles 4, 5, 6 and 7 (file styles 5-9). HELD, NOT SHIPPED: page Style 8 (European; page states it cannot be decoded from any known chart).

styles.era: 1980-1982, 7-character serials with year letter first or last (page Style 4)
styles.notes: Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): the year letter may occur at the beginning or the end of the serial; this is the letter-first form. Table: A or O = 1980, B or T = 1981, C or U = 1982. The image says 1980-1982; the page text says 1981-1983 -- the chart table governs. ORDERING: these two exact 7-character styles sit first in the file, ahead of the open-ended digit-led style-2, so a 7-character digit-led serial with a trailing letter decodes as this 1980-1982 system rather than as a 2010+ digit-led serial; a 2010+ serial in exactly this shape would decode here instead, a documented page ambiguity the data plate must disambiguate.

styles.era: 1980-1982, 7-character serials with year letter first or last (page Style 4)
styles.notes: Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): letter-last form of page Style 4. See style-5 notes for the table and the ordering rationale.

Year-prefix range 10-26 in the pattern must be extended as the calendar advances; the century rule alone would misread pre-2010 digit-led serials. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2010+ reading) and style-1 (2002-2009 reading); this style is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading. The page notes the styles overlap and directs techs to the data-plate MFR date to disambiguate; a 2002 serial in the overlap set will decode as a 2020s year.

Single-digit year encoded as a digit-keyed letterTable because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the mapping (digit d = 2000+d for 2002-2009) is the page's stated rule. CAVEAT: the page notes some circa 1978-79 models may have used this shape, so a leading 8 or 9 could be 1978/1979 on a very old unit; condition and appearance disambiguate per the page. ORDERING: digit-led serials starting 20-26 match BOTH this style (2002-2009 reading) and style-2 (2010+ reading); style-2 is tried first, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading and the data-plate MFR date must disambiguate per the page. A 2002 serial in the overlap set therefore decodes as a 2020s year; this is a documented page ambiguity, not a silent guess.

Letter table: the page's chart is an image that text fetch cannot OCR. Anchors confirmed in page text: S = 1986, Z = 2001, F = 1991 (page example F23456789, 23rd week of 1991), C = 1988 (page example C01D47415, 1st week of 1988); header examples are consistent with R = 2000 and M = 1997. Remaining mappings corroborated by independent published Trane charts. CHART-VERIFIED (image-pass Nov 8): the page's own year chart lists L = 1996, so the page text's claim that A, I, L, O and Q were not used is wrong about L; A genuinely has no entry. L = 1996 stays. The page warns this style is easily confused with page styles 3, 4, 6 and 7.

styles.era: 1970s onward, factory letter + 2-digit year + month letter, 9 characters (page Style 3)
styles.notes: Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): the page's chart supplies the month table (A January through M December, I skipped), so month is now encoded; the example decodes as December 1992. The page warns this style is easily confused with page Style 2; ordering (letter-year style tried first) plus week-range validation resolves most collisions, since a page-Style-3 serial whose factory letter is in the year table and whose year digits are 01-53 would otherwise decode as a letter-year serial.

Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): year is the 1st digit, month is the 2nd letter. Single-digit year encoded as an explicit digit-keyed table because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the chart bounds the era to 1971-1979. The page text mentions possible early-1980s reuse for limited products, but no mapping is given for it.

styles.era: 1980s, letter + 6 digits + year letter + 2-digit week (page Style 6)
styles.notes: Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): year is the third-to-last character, week is the last two digits. The L/M/N letters the file note said were unmapped are in this chart (A, L, or O = 1980; B, M, or T = 1981; C, N, or U = 1982). NOTE: this 10-character pattern does not overlap shipped style-3's 9-character pattern, so no ordering trade-off applies; it sits after style-3 in file order.

styles.era: 1970s into the 1990s, month letter + 2-digit year + 5 digits (page Style 7)
styles.notes: Chart-verified (image-pass Nov 8): month is the 1st letter, year is the 2nd-3rd digits. 'Generally used from the 70's into the 90's' per the page.
